A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VGGSounder benchmark. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including v3's added changelog.

before.justification: V1 reports original annotation audits, evaluations of eleven audio-visual models, and supplementary sensitivity and label-source analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised modality-confusion results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The label-proposal pipeline, human annotation, label aggregation, evaluated model architectures, and prediction procedures remain unchanged. The revision concerns evaluation metrics rather than the underlying method or models.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same VGGSound/VGGSounder data and modality and confounder scenarios. Perception Test and EPIC-Sounds are added as related benchmarks, without reported training or evaluation on them.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain four embedding models, three Gemini models, and four open-source foundation models. No evaluated comparator is added or removed, including within the appendix studies.

E3.justification: Appendix D.6 explicitly revises modality confusion: multimodal predictions are now checked against all available labels rather than only AV labels. Other reported evaluation settings, including top-k choices and prompting protocols, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing confounder and annotation-source analyses receive revised modality-confusion evidence in Tables 8–14 and 16–17, changing their characterization of fusion failures. The tested factors remain unchanged; Table 18 reproduces earlier results rather than introducing another robustness test.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seed-based variation, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Annotation-agreement reporting and descriptive statistics retain the same reporting practices.

E6.justification: Revised μ results substantially alter a central diagnostic pattern: Table 2 changes from three of four embedding models having μA below μV to three having μA above μV. Gemini 1.5 Flash's μA changes from 10.22 to 14.36. Table 3 also revises the 'neither' differences, including CAV-MAE's joint ΔF1 from −4.65 to −1.24. Most classification scores remain stable; the μ values use different definitions and do not establish model performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix D.6 revises the label-based correctness condition defining μ. Equation (1) also replaces m(x) with a(x), although the surrounding text still defines m as audio or visual, leaving the visual case inconsistent. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about modality-aware relabelling, foundation-model evaluation, modality confusion, and confounder analysis.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations are retained. In particular, Section 5.1 still says most embedding models reverse the foundation models' modality-confusion pattern, although the revised Table 2 no longer supports that statement.

D1.justification: Appendix D.6 adds implementation history and a version-specific reference to the old metric implementation in package version 0.1.4.1. Existing annotation instructions, checkpoint descriptions, evaluator configuration, and prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Table 1 add Perception Test and EPIC-Sounds, acknowledging their modality annotations while distinguishing their class coverage and egocentric scope. This is a limited expansion of research positioning.

P1.justification: V3 adds a short related-work passage and Appendix D.6, standardizes appendix references, and makes limited wording and bibliography corrections. The main narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 2–4 are redrawn with revised typography and spacing while retaining their examples and plotted information. Table 1 gains two rows, and new Table 18 redisplays v1's Table 2; accompanying page-flow changes are limited.

improvement.justification: The added benchmark context, metric changelog, and preserved legacy results improve context and traceability. However, v3 introduces an inconsistency in Equation (1) and leaves a central interpretation in Section 5.1 contradicted by its revised Table 2. These unresolved issues concern the metric being refined, so the PDFs do not establish whether the benefits outweigh the loss of mathematical and interpretive consistency.
